---
id: SA-0297
title: SA-0290's removed-name clash restates a whole-word matcher, reads bare from subject-equals-path, and leaves build_queue's own docstring silent on the ninth refusal
type: bug
priority: 3
estimated_lines: 130
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - saffron/scheduler.py
  - tests/test_scheduler.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/cli.py
  - saffron/task.py
  - saffron/batch.py
  - saffron/ledger.py
  - saffron/intake.py
  - saffron/repos/**
  - saffron/agents/**
  - saffron/phases/**
  - saffron/gates/**
  - saffron/cell/**
  - tests/test_cli.py
  - tests/test_intake.py
  - tests/test_refusal_count.py
  - tests/test_revert.py
  - tests/test_queued_specs.py
  - tests/test_consumes.py
  - tests/test_mirror.py
budget_usd: 15
max_attempts: 2
max_turns: 60
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      A removed name's whole-word match reuses `saffron.repos.mirror`'s
      `_word_pattern`, the helper `unresolved_consumes` already calls for a
      `consumes` entry's name, rather than a third local copy of the same
      lookaround. `saffron/scheduler.py` declares no `_whole_word` and no
      `_WORD_BOUNDARY` of its own, and its own `_word_pattern` name is the
      identical object `mirror._word_pattern` is. The match stays whole-word,
      with no letter, digit or underscore on either side, and case sensitive.
    witness: tests/test_scheduler.py::test_the_removed_name_matcher_reuses_mirrors_word_pattern
    mutant:
      file: saffron/scheduler.py
      find: 'from saffron.repos.mirror import _word_pattern'
      replace: "from saffron.repos.mirror import _word_pattern as _mirror_word_pattern\n\n\ndef _word_pattern(name: str):\n    return _mirror_word_pattern(name)"
    wrong_versions:
      - A fourth local pattern written under a new name, so `mirror.py`'s and `scheduler.py`'s whole-word rules can still drift apart.
      - The `\b`-bounded `_names_whole_word` from `witness.py` imported instead, whose boundary reads a path's own dot or slash differently than `mirror.py`'s character class does.
      - The import added, but one call site still reads the old local name, so the module fails to load.
      - The compiled pattern cached once at import time, keyed on the first subject seen, so `_word_pattern`'s second call reuses the first subject's pattern.
  - claim: >-
      A `removes` entry's `bare` reading comes from whether the entry itself
      held a colon, never from comparing its resolved subject to its path.
      An entry like `pkg/thing.py:pkg/thing.py`, whose declared name equals
      its own path, reads as named, not bare, so a reader whose `consumes`
      entry shares that path under a different name does not clash on the
      path half alone.
    witness: tests/test_scheduler.py::test_a_removes_entry_naming_its_own_path_is_not_read_as_bare
    mutant:
      file: saffron/scheduler.py
      find: '        bare = ":" not in entry'
      replace: '        bare = subject == path'
    wrong_versions:
      - The flag kept as `subject == path`, so a `path:name` entry whose declared name equals its own path still reads as bare.
      - The flag read from whether `"/"` sits in the entry instead, so a bare entry under a nested path like `pkg/sub/thing.py` reads as named.
      - The flag read from the reader's `consumes` entry instead of the remover's `removes` entry, so it never reflects what the remover itself declared.
  - claim: >-
      `build_queue`'s own docstring, not only the module docstring above it,
      names the removed-name clash it also refuses on: a ninth
      `depends_on` site, from backlog item b-e773d9. A reader of the
      function alone, without reading the module docstring, learns of this
      check.
    witness: tests/test_scheduler.py::test_build_queues_own_docstring_names_the_removed_name_refusal
    mutant:
      file: saffron/scheduler.py
      find: "a ninth `depends_on` site from\n    backlog item b-e773d9."
      replace: "a parent one lacks."
    wrong_versions:
      - The sentence stays only in the module docstring, so a reader of `build_queue` alone still learns nothing of the ninth refusal, the defect as filed.
      - A sentence naming "a ninth `depends_on` site" but not "removed name", so a reader learns a count grew without learning what grew it.
      - A sentence naming the clash but citing no backlog item, breaking the trail every other paragraph in this docstring keeps.
---

## Context

Reviewer findings on `SA-0290` (`b78b0d3c`), this stack's prior layer. Line
numbers below were read at this stack's head, `c6a511eb`, where that diff
sits in `saffron/scheduler.py` unchanged by either spec that landed after it.

**The restated matcher.** `saffron/scheduler.py:710-717` defines
`_WORD_BOUNDARY` and `_whole_word`, a whole-word search over the pattern
`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])`, the escaped subject, `(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`.
`saffron/repos/mirror.py:297-298` already defines `_word_pattern`, built
from the identical character class and the identical lookaround over the
escaped name. `mirror.py`'s `unresolved_consumes`
(`saffron/repos/mirror.py:301-324`) calls it at line 321, to check a
`path:name` `consumes` entry against a tree's file text. A third
independent copy of the same rule sits in `saffron/gates/core/witness.py`,
whose `_names_whole_word` (`saffron/gates/core/witness.py:418-419`) uses
`\b` rather than the explicit character class, for a constant's name
rather than a path or a name that can hold a dot or a slash.
`saffron/repos/mirror.py` imports only `saffron.cell.worktree`, and
`saffron/scheduler.py` imports `saffron.cell.session`,
`saffron.gates.core.scope`, `saffron.intake` and `saffron.ledger`. No
import cycle stands between the two. Other modules already import a
private, underscore-prefixed name across this same boundary:
`saffron/qualify.py:29` and `saffron/spec_citations.py:16` both import
`_git` from `saffron.repos.mirror`.

**The bare misread.** `saffron/scheduler.py:720-740` defines
`_removed_name_clash`. Line 730 reads `path, subject =
_entry_subject(entry)`, where `_entry_subject`
(`saffron/scheduler.py:697-704`) returns `name or path` as the subject.
Line 731 then reads `bare = subject == path`. An entry such as
`pkg/thing.py:pkg/thing.py`, whose declared name happens to equal its own
path, makes `subject == path` true even though the entry names a subject
explicitly. Line 738's `if bare and consumed_path == path` then matches any
reader `consumes` entry whose path half is that path, whatever name that
entry actually declares, a clash the spec's own rule for a bare removed
path, in `SA-0290`'s fourth acceptance criterion, does not call for. No
test in `SA-0290`'s diff drives an entry where the declared name equals
the path.

**The silent docstring.** `SA-0290`'s task body asked for a sentence in
`build_queue`'s own docstring, beside a paragraph in the module docstring.
The module docstring's paragraph landed at `saffron/scheduler.py:40-49`,
naming the ninth `depends_on` site, backlog item b-e773d9 and the reason
the refusal avoids the field's name. `build_queue`'s own docstring
(`saffron/scheduler.py:1155-1209`) still ends, at line 1208, on the
sentence about `stack=True` and `_stack_order`, with no sentence of its
own on the removed-name clash. `build_queue`
(`saffron/scheduler.py:1305-1333`) now computes `_removed_name_refusals`
and appends its `Refusal` under the `depends_on` kind before the
per-candidate loop runs. A reader of `build_queue` alone, without first
reading the module docstring forty lines above it, has no way to learn
that the function now performs this ninth check.

## Problem

Fix the three defects the review found in `SA-0290`'s removed-name clash,
each confined to `saffron/scheduler.py` and its tests.

**Reuse, not a third copy.** Delete `_WORD_BOUNDARY` and `_whole_word` from
`saffron/scheduler.py`. Import `_word_pattern` from `saffron.repos.mirror`
and call it everywhere `_whole_word` was called, keeping the same
whole-word, case-sensitive behavior `_removed_name_clash` already has.

**Read `bare` from the entry's own shape.** Replace `bare = subject ==
path` with a test of whether `entry` itself held a colon. Keep
`_entry_subject`'s own signature and its callers for `consumes` entries
unchanged. Only the `removes` entry's `bare` flag changes.

**Document the ninth check where it runs.** Add one sentence to
`build_queue`'s own docstring naming the removed-name clash as a refusal it
performs, citing backlog item b-e773d9, the same item the module docstring
already cites. Leave the module docstring's paragraph as it reads at base.

Write the three new tests the criteria name, in `tests/test_scheduler.py`.
No other file in `touches` needs a change to satisfy them, but `tests/test_scheduler.py`'s
imports gain `inspect`, `saffron.scheduler` itself (for the identity check)
and `saffron.repos.mirror`.

## Out of scope

- **`saffron/gates/core/witness.py`'s own `_names_whole_word`.** It serves a
  different caller, over constant names rather than paths, and its `\b`
  boundary is not this spec's to touch.
- **`DESIGN.md` §4.2.1 and `CONTEXT.md`.** Neither changed meaning here.
  The refusal still reads as the same ninth `depends_on` site, only
  documented and implemented more carefully.
- **Any other finding on `SA-0290`'s diff not named above.** This spec is
  scoped to the three the review raised.

## Notes for the agent

**Every criterion edits code that already exists at base**, so every
criterion declares a mechanical `mutant` alongside its `wrong_versions`.
`witness` will not report `skip` for any of them.

**The identity check is the point of the first witness.** A mutant that
keeps `_word_pattern`'s own behavior, but reintroduces a second object
under the same name, still passes a witness that only checks matching.
The shadowing import this spec's own `mutant` field drives is exactly that
case. So the witness asserts
`scheduler._word_pattern is git_mirror._word_pattern` directly, rather
than only re-driving `test_a_removed_name_matches_only_as_a_whole_word`'s
cases.

**The second witness's fixture needs a `depends_on`.** The reader's
`consumes` entry needs a parent merged at `TE-0`, the same pattern
`test_a_removed_name_is_read_from_the_body_the_claims_and_consumes` already
uses for its `consumes`-bearing cases.

**The `prose` gate** counts each new comment and docstring. Write none with
an em dash, a semicolon, a contraction, the perfect tense or a sentence
over 25 words, the sentence added to `build_queue`'s docstring included.

**Size.** A prototype measured 429 changed tokens total, 129 of them
outside `tests/**`, against the `bug` ceiling of 1300. Every test in
`tests/test_scheduler.py` passed on it, and so did the three new ones.
